edges.description: VAX1 is required in anterior midline cells to guide commissural axons; its loss removes attractive guidance cues from those cells.

nodes.description: VAX1 is expressed in anterior midline cells that orchestrate axon trajectories. In the Vax1 null mouse, axons of the corpus callosum and the hippocampal and anterior commissures fail to cross the midline, because the normally Vax1-positive midline cells show markedly diminished expression of attractive guidance cues (the cells survive; the defect is in their guidance function).

nodes.description: In the Vax1 null mouse, loss of Vax1 causes a proximal expansion of Pax6 and Rx activity in the developing visual system and defects in the basal telencephalon, indicating that Vax1 normally restrains dorsal eye-field programs and specifies ventral forebrain/optic-stalk identity. This is mouse evidence applied to the human disorder by phenocopy.

meta.association: Biallelic VAX1 variants cause MCOPS11. The reported allele is a homozygous dinucleotide substitution (c.453G>A and c.454C>A) predicting the missense change p.Arg152Ser at an invariant residue of the VAX1 homeodomain. The authors favour loss of function because the human phenotype resembles the Vax1 homozygous null mouse. VAX1 is one of the established genes of the microphthalmia-anophthalmia-coloboma (MAC) spectrum.

evidence.snippet: This review will focus on MAC phenotypes that are associated with mutation of the genes SOX2, OTX2, PAX6, STRA6, ALDH1A3, RARB, VSX2, RAX, FOXE3, BMP4, BMP7, GDF3, GDF6, ABCB6, ATOH7, C12orf57, TENM3 (ODZ3), and VAX1.

nodes.description: A homozygous missense change at an invariant residue of the VAX1 homeodomain (p.Arg152Ser) is the initiating lesion. VAX1 is a homeodomain transcription factor that binds DNA sequence-specifically; the lesion is predicted to reduce its DNA-binding transcription-factor activity. Loss of function is the authors' interpretation, inferred from the human phenotype resembling the Vax1 homozygous null mouse rather than from an assay of this allele.
